chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad al-Bandaniji narrated from Ubayd Allah ibn Musa al-Alawi, from one who narrated it, from Ja'far ibn Yahya, from his father, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he said:
"How will you be if the companions of al-Qa'im set up their pavilions in the mosque of Kufa, and then he appears to them with a new ideal, a new matter, severe upon the Arabs."

key_terms.الْفَسَاطِيط: Pavilions or tents, indicating establishment of authority
key_terms.الْقَائِم: The Riser, a title for the Twelfth Imam
key_terms.الْمِثَالُ الْمُسْتَأْنَفُ: The new ideal or model, referring to his unique governance
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ كُوفَانَ: The mosque of Kufa, a key location in Shia eschatology

ai.seo_question: What characterizes the leadership of al-Qa'im when he appears?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq emphasizes the dramatic and transformative nature of the Mahdi's rise, specifically noting the striking of drums (fasatit) in Kufa's mosque as a signal of mobilization. The 'new example' (al-Mithal al-Mustanaf) refers to a novel political and spiritual authority that will be formidable to the Arab tribes, reflecting the Shia eschatological expectation of a decisive break from previous historical patterns. This event marks the establishment of global justice, fulfilling the covenant of divine vicegerency.
